regressionChecked: MEDIUM finding from the prior round (mobile duplicate-message bug) verified fixed: use-qa-thread.ts:66-69 now computes `known = new Set(history.items.map(m => m.id))` and filters sentMessages against it before combining, so a history refetch that already contains a just-sent turn (e.g. the app foregrounding mid-thread) no longer renders it twice. New test use-qa-thread.test.tsx:98-117 ('shows a sent turn once when a history refetch ... already contains it') re-renders with a history page containing the sent question/answer pair and asserts items are exactly ['q1','a1'] — traced the assertion against the actual filter logic, not just the test's own mock: without the `known` filter this would produce ['q1','a1','q1','a1'], matching what I originally found.

New: qa.integration.spec.ts:187-200 proves the budget-exhaustion path end to end — a user with monthly_token_budget=10 and 10 tokens already recorded in usage_records gets a 429 HttpException with code QUOTA_EXCEEDED from askGlobal, AND qa.history afterward is empty, proving the transaction genuinely never partially commits a question/answer pair when the AI call is rejected before generation.

New: qa.integration.spec.ts:279-299 replace what were previously any-typed monkeypatches of private internals with real fake-Gemini reply sequences — 'not even json' then a malformed JSON object then a valid one correctly retries 3 times and stores the eventual good answer; three consecutive malformed replies correctly exhausts ANSWER_ATTEMPTS, throws 503, and — like the quota case — leaves qa.history empty. This closes a gap from the first round: I had not previously seen the schema-retry path proven against the real parseAnswer/generateText loop rather than a mocked one.

New: qa.integration.spec.ts:202-225 (unit-level) and qa.e2e.spec.ts:107-120 (HTTP-level) both drive three-plus questions and walk the `before` cursor across multiple pages, confirming next_before chains correctly and the final page's next_before is null — the pagination contract (created_at, id) tuple ordering holds under a real multi-page walk, not just a single boundary check.

New: qa.integration.spec.ts:227-243 proves DELETE /meetings/:id/qa only clears that meeting's thread — a second meeting's history is untouched, closing a gap the first round did not explicitly check (only single-thread clear/read had been proven before).

Renamed-not-rewritten: qa.e2e.spec.ts:95 ('marks a stored citation unavailable once its passage is gone') is the same assertion as the prior round's misnamed version — confirmed the test body is unchanged beyond the name, so this is a naming fix, not new coverage.

Removed: a duplicate dayBound unit test and a vacuous budget-truncation test (only one chunk ever in scope, so truncation was never exercised) were deleted; qa-core.spec.ts:18-32 already covers the real truncation case (a 5000-word chunk forced against a 100-token budget) so no coverage was lost.

temper-results.json read directly, all real exit codes: 8/8 pass — api unit 387 (+10 from last round), e2e 130 (+3), schema 5, mobile 1051 (+1, the new use-qa-thread dedup test), both typechecks and eslint --max-warnings=0 clean.
